MasterChef star returns to King’s Lynn for special menu
MasterChef: The Professionals semi-finalist Polly Norman has returned to her roots in Norfolk for two special evenings at King’s Lynn Golf Club. The 24-year-old from Upwell, who began her career at the club as a teenager, teamed up with head chef Liam Nicol to prepare a four-course menu featuring local game and coastal produce.
Polly, who now works at Simpson’s in the Strand in London, previously worked as an assistant professional at the golf club before pursuing a culinary career. She says she hopes to eventually return to the county permanently to open her own gastropub on the Norfolk coast.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Campaign launches to improve child visibility as clocks go back
A new safety initiative, Be Bright Be Seen, is offering thousands of free reflective keyrings to schools, youth groups, and sports clubs across the region. Sponsored by Ashwood Homes, the campaign aims to help children remain visible to motorists as the nights draw in. With the clocks changing this Sunday, October 25, organisers are encouraging the use of reflective gear and bright clothing for pedestrians and cyclists.
Teachers and youth leaders can apply for an allocation of the keyrings online at the Fenland Citizen website. Applications close this Sunday. The campaign follows recent national data highlighting a rise in road traffic injuries, emphasising the importance of staying visible during the darker winter months.

item.title: South Lynn man admits assault following domestic dispute
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
South Lynn man admits assault following domestic dispute
A 48-year-old man from South Lynn has pleaded guilty to common assault at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Cornelius Doddy, of Wisbech Road, admitted to threatening his ex-partner with an ironing board during an argument on July 29. The court heard that the dispute began in a car and continued at their home, where the defendant was reportedly intoxicated. No injuries were sustained during the incident.
In mitigation, the court was told that tensions regarding a potential restaurant venture had contributed to the disagreement. Magistrates have ordered a pre-sentence report, and Mr Doddy has been released on conditional bail. He is due to return to court for sentencing on December 1.

item.title: West Norfolk schools support mental health campaign
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk schools support mental health campaign
Pupils and staff across several West Norfolk schools have marked World Mental Health Day by taking part in the ‘Hello Yellow’ campaign. Participants wore bright colours to raise awareness and funds for the charity Young Minds. At West Lynn Primary School, children and staff held a special assembly and completed mental health-related classroom activities.
Other schools within the West Norfolk Academies Trust also joined the initiative, including Smithdon High School in Hunstanton, St Clement’s High School in Terrington St Clement, and Clenchwarton Primary. The schools shared donation links via their newsletters and websites to support the charity’s work. West Lynn Primary typically raises around £200 for the cause during this annual event.
